findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The direct write may be deliberate telemetry sanctioned while the mode is on legacy authority and consumed only before any later append; that reading fails because fanout-merge runs after the lineage settles and a retry attempt's append can precede it, and the shipped guard classifies the same bytes as a violation once authority flips.
findingDetails.claim: The fan-out salvage sweep writes deep-review-state.jsonl directly, bypassing the append gateway, so its event is not ledger-backed, is erased by the next gateway projection refresh, and reads as a gateway-bypass violation under ledger authority.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether mergeJsonlUnderLock is a gateway-backed writer (raw locked rewrite, jsonl-repair.ts:282); whether the projection preserves direct rows (digest-valid prefix only, shadow-projection-store.ts:556-577); whether the guard treats this as sanctioned (not-enforced only while legacy_authoritative, check-direct-append.cjs:145-172); the unit test asserts the row lands but never re-appends through the gateway afterwards.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if a documented authority exemption states fan-out salvage may write the projection directly under all authority states, or if the salvage event moves off the projection while the guard is updated to exempt this writer.
findingDetails.evidence: Post-exit salvage writes its salvaged_from_stdout event with mergeJsonlUnderLock(stateLogPath, [eventRecord]) (fanout-salvage.cjs:162-171), a raw locked JSONL rewrite (lib/deep-loop/jsonl-repair.ts:282-296 -> writeJsonlRecordsAtomic), not an append through append-mode-event.cjs. The gateway refreshes the projection from the ledger after every authorized append and shadow-projection-store.ts:548-577 appends a true suffix or writeTextAtomic-replaces the whole file; a direct row breaks the watermark digest, so the next gateway append replaces the projection and the salvage row is dropped. fanout-merge.cjs:966 reads salvaged_from_stdout from the same projection for its attribution table, so a retried or resumed lineage reports zero salvage. Under ledger authority, check-direct-append.cjs:223-253 compares the legacy file digest against the gateway watermark and reports status violation for exactly this divergence.
findingDetails.recommendation: Emit the salvage event through the append gateway under a deep_review stem (or record it in the delta), keeping the projection ledger-owned; add a test that appends through the gateway after salvage and asserts the event survives.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read the full salvage path, the raw writer it calls, the projection refresh that owns the same file, the guard that detects divergence, and the merge consumer that reads the event.
findingDetails.title: Fan-out salvage appends to the lineage state log directly instead of through the append gateway

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The window may be judged too short and the losing run's heartbeat eventually notices the mismatch; neither closes the hole because the window contains a temp write plus fsync, a descheduled process can be delayed arbitrarily inside it, and the heartbeat check happens after both acquisitions and does not force either run to stand down.
findingDetails.claim: tryReclaimStaleLoopLock can replace a fresh lock published by another reclaimer, so two concurrent acquirers can both return acquired:true and both write the same review packet.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the reclaim re-reads and verifies the claimed record (it does not); whether link-based publish forces EEXIST on the loser (only when the loser has not itself vacated lockPath first); whether ENOENT protects the winner (only if the loser's rename lands while lockPath is absent); whether hostLocalSingleFlight serializes production callers (tests only); whether a test interleaves two reclaimers (the atomic-publish test races fresh acquire against an observer).
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to P2 if the acquire CLI enables hostLocalSingleFlight or the reclaim verifies the renamed record's identity and restores an unverified fresh lock untouched, with an interleaving test.
findingDetails.evidence: tryReclaimStaleLoopLock renames whatever is at lockPath to a private claim path and republishes its own record without verifying that the renamed record is the stale holder observed at :456-457. A second caller that read the same stale holder can rename and replace the fresh lock published by the first reclaimer: A.rename -> A.writeLoopLockExclusive (temp write + fsync + link, :265-286) -> B.rename -> B.link yields two acquired:true results. The comment claiming two reclaimers can never both hold the lock only covers racing on the same stale inode. The host-local single-flight backstop is engaged only when options.hostLocalSingleFlight === true (:600-603), which scripts/loop-lock.cjs:156 never passes. deep-review-auto.yaml:297-298 fails closed only when acquired=false, so two runs can write the same packet; the loser's heartbeat later stops silently on identity mismatch.
findingDetails.recommendation: Verify the renamed record against the observed stale holder before republishing (compare owner pid, nonce, heartbeat) and restore a fresh lock untouched; or wire hostLocalSingleFlight into the acquire CLI; add a test that interleaves two reclaimers of one stale lock and asserts a single winner.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read the full lock library, the CLI that calls it, the fence-capability consumer, the concurrency unit test, and the workflow acquire/release steps; the reclaim rename is the only unverified mutation in the lifecycle.
findingDetails.title: Two processes can both reclaim the same stale loop lock and both hold the packet lock

findingDetails.evidence: The child loop (validate.sh:378-394) skips any [0-9][0-9][0-9]-* directory that is non-empty but has neither spec.md nor description.json, then aggregates only validated children. The exemption targets artifact-only children (review/, research/, as the comment at :382-384 says), and a read-only walk shows every currently skipped child is that kind; the unhandled state is a phase whose spec.md and description.json are both absent while plan.md/tasks.md remain, which the parent reports as RESULT: PASSED without naming the skipped child.
findingDetails.recommendation: Narrow the skip predicate (e.g. require that the child's top level holds only artifact directories or changelog markdown) or print the skipped numbered children in the report so a parent run cannot pass over an invalid child silently.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Read the recursive loop and its skip predicate end to end, then walked the spec tree for children matched by the predicate; all observed matches are artifact-only directories, so the gap is latent rather than exercised today.
